@graph.name: Urban Pluvial Flood Risk Toolbox
@graph.description: A modular and configurable Python toolbox for urban pluvial flood risk assessment. Implements the IPCC risk framework (Risk = Hazard × Exposure × Vulnerability) to produce two risk indices: PFRMA (mobility & accessibility) and PFRWB (well-being).

@graph.name: Urban Pluvial Flood Risk Analysis
@graph.description: Entry point for the urban pluvial flood risk assessment pipeline. Orchestrates validation, social vulnerability analysis (TOPSIS), exposure calculation, hazard metrics, risk combination, and visualization.

@graph.name: urban_pfr package
@graph.description: Python package implementing the pluvial flood risk pipeline modules: validation, indicators (TOPSIS), exposure, hazard, risk, and visualization.

@graph.name: buildings_gdb
@graph.description: ArcGIS File Geodatabase containing the core spatial datasets: building footprints with attributes (residential area, floors, building type), statistical units with demographic indicators (sensitivity and coping capacity fields), and street network outlines.

@graph.name: buildings
@graph.description: Building footprints with attributes (residential area, floors, building type). Alternative to buildings_gdb when inputs are provided as individual files.

@graph.name: statistical_units
@graph.description: Statistical units with demographic indicators (sensitivity and coping capacity fields).

@graph.name: streets
@graph.description: Street network outlines for hazard mobility and accessibility analysis.

@graph.name: flood_levels
@graph.description: Directory of geospatial files representing pluvial flood depth scenarios. Each file covers one depth level (e.g. 30cm, 40cm, ... 100cm). Supported formats: FlatGeobuf, GeoJSON, Shapefile, GeoPackage.

@graph.name: config
@graph.description: YAML configuration file specifying project settings (CRS, city name), schema field mappings, hazard parameters (buffer distances, flood threshold), risk weights, TOPSIS weights, and visualization options.

@graph.name: boundary
@graph.description: Study area boundary polygon used to clip the analysis extent. If not provided, the convex hull of the building footprints is used.

@graph.name: elderly_singles
@graph.description: Count of elderly singles (65+) per statistical unit

@graph.name: children
@graph.description: Count of children under 10 per statistical unit

@graph.name: welfare_recipients
@graph.description: Count of welfare recipients per statistical unit

@graph.name: education_quota
@graph.description: Count of people without high school diploma per statistical unit

@graph.name: residents
@graph.description: Total resident count per statistical unit

@graph.name: living_area
@graph.description: Total housing area per statistical unit (m²)

@graph.name: floors
@graph.description: Number of floors per building

@graph.name: building_type
@graph.description: Building use type (1=residential, 2=mixed-use)

@graph.name: statistical_unit
@graph.description: Statistical unit identifier for spatial aggregation

@graph.name: risk_layer
@graph.description: Building-level flood risk indices (PFRMA for mobility/accessibility, PFRWB for well-being) as Thiessen polygons with Delaunay-smoothed variants. Contains columns: RIMA, RIWB, RIMA_smooth, RIWB_smooth.

@graph.name: vulnerability_layer
@graph.description: Statistical units with social vulnerability indicators: Sensitivity, Coping Capacity, Social Vulnerability Index (SVI), and flood-specific vulnerability (SVPF).

@graph.name: Hamburg configuration
@graph.description: Example YAML configuration for the Hamburg case study (CS3).
